title: Random XOR
statementMd:
You are given n integers a1,a2,…,an and two integers m and k. For each position i, independently choose an integer di (0≤di≤k) and replace its value with ai+di.

For every 0≤s<2m, count the choices satisfying

(a1+d1)⊕⋯⊕(an+dn)=s.

Here, ⊕ denotes the bitwise XOR operation. Write the two nonnegative integers in binary and pad them with leading zeros to the same length. For each position, the resulting bit is 1 if the two corresponding bits differ, and 0 if they are equal. For example, (0011)2⊕(0101)2=(0110)2.

Two choices are different if and only if the chosen increments differ at at least one position. Print all answers modulo 998 244 353.

## Input

There is only one test case in each test file.

The first line contains three integers n, m, k (1≤n≤500000, 1≤m≤19, 0≤k≤100). It is guaranteed that 2m−k>0.

The second line contains n integers a1,a2,…,an (0≤ai<2m−k).

## Output

Print 2m integers. The j-th integer is the number of choices for s=j−1, modulo 998 244 353.

## Note

In the first example, the first number can become 0 or 1, and the second can become 1 or 2. The four choices give XOR values 1,2,0,3, so all answers are 1.
